page.layout: One printed page, text block in the centre-right of the scan. Running head at top; page number 154 at top left of the text. Body in justified lines, with the last lines centred as a short indented block (verse-like lines of the Maii passage), then a catchword "De" at the lower right. No margin notes.

main_text.p: Franciæ quàm Burgundiæ PLACITVM REGA-LE, diuersorúmque conuentus principum Suef-sionis habetur. ad quod impediendum (si fieri potest) Richardus filius Wilhelmi Nortmanni accedens, à fidelibus Regis quibusdam perua-sus, & interemptis suorum nonnullis in fugam conuersus est. Sed singula testimonia persequi laboris esset infiniti, &, vt opinor, superuaca-nei. Nam ex iis quę vsque adhuc protulimus pa-tere cuiuis arbitramur, iudicium arbitriúmque summæ Reipub. vsque ad Carolum Simplicem, hoc est, per annos amplius quingentos & quin-quaginta penes populi comitia, & (vt nunc loqui-mur) statuum siue Ordinum conuentum fuis-se: idque Maiorum nostrorum institutum pro sacrosanćto habitum tot seculis fuisse: vt iam Scriptorum quorundam recentium satis admi-rari iudicium non possim, quos non est pudi-tum, suis in libellis tradere, Concilij publici in-stitutum Pipino Regi accepto ferendum esse: cùm Eguinarthus Caroli Magni Cancellarius tam dilucidè testetur, Merouingiorum omniū institutum fuisse, vt quotannis Kalend. Maij publicum populi sui conuétum agerent, ad eumque conuen-tnm carpento bobus tracto vehe-ŗentur.

page.notes: Lower right corner shows a catchword "De". The printed text is partly dense and the scan is slightly skewed; "conuentum" and "tnm" and "ŗentur" in the verse-like lines are the printed forms (likely "conuentum", "tum", "vehentur" misprinted). Doubtful: "Eguinarthus" and "Merouingiorum" are as printed.
